title: Tech Note: Inexpensive Wireless Status Display Solution with 4D
author: Vance Villanueva, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This is a hardware/IoT hobbyist-style tutorial (Arduino IDE, WeMos ESP8266, I2C LCD wiring) whose core idea — a 4D method serving status data over the 4D Web Server to a cheap WiFi microcontroller display — remains architecturally valid, though specific product links (AliExpress listings), driver URLs, and Arduino board-manager steps are highly likely to have gone stale or changed since 2017. The general microcontroller/IoT ecosystem has also evolved substantially (newer ESP32/ESP8266 variants, updated Arduino IDE versions), so exact steps would need revalidation, but 4D's role (a Web Server method returning status data) is unaffected by 4D's own product evolution.
related_updates: 4D Web Server method-based status endpoint pattern is still valid today
Specific hardware links, driver download URLs, and Arduino IDE/board-manager steps from 2017 are likely outdated
Newer/cheaper microcontroller boards (e.g., ESP32) have since become more common than the WeMos ESP8266 featured here
